patches.reason: The current fullscreen mode maximizes the whole PreviewPane, including its toolbar and runtime console, so the project itself does not occupy the complete screen. Convert fullscreen/maximized mode into a true project viewport: the iframe covers the entire visual viewport edge-to-edge, viewer chrome and runtime diagnostics are removed, and only a small floating exit-fullscreen button remains above the project so fullscreen can still be closed on desktop, Android, iOS Safari, and installed home-screen mode.

iOS Safari does not always treat vh/dvh/svh consistently inside srcdoc iframes, especially with the browser chrome, orientation changes, virtual keyboard, and installed home-screen mode. CDE projects commonly use viewport units for page shells, fixed panels, modals, onboarding screens, and dashboards. Normalize those units against runtime visual-viewport CSS variables so every CDE project's existing CSS follows the actual visible iOS viewport without project-specific changes.

Apply the cross-browser viewport normalization to the complete CDE stylesheet aggregate so fullscreen shells, fixed docks, dashboards, modals, login pages, onboarding pages, and other viewport-sized layouts use the actual iOS visual viewport.

The CDE iframe currently depends on CSS viewport units alone. On iOS Safari those values can differ from the actually visible iframe viewport while browser bars collapse, the keyboard appears, orientation changes, or the viewer runs from the home screen. Establish runtime viewport variables and a stable scrolling/root contract that CDE CSS can consume while preserving each project's own styling.

Synchronize the generated CDE document with Safari's visualViewport before any project store, boot logic, React render, or layout measurement executes. Keep it synchronized through address-bar movement, rotation, resize, keyboard appearance, page restoration, and home-screen resume. This fixes CDE pages that calculate their initial mobile layout only once during application boot.

The outer viewer has the same Safari visual-viewport problem as the project iframe. Synchronize its CSS viewport variables with visualViewport so the mobile project selector, workspace, preview region, fullscreen fallback, modals, browser chrome changes, orientation, and installed-home-screen mode all use the actual visible iOS dimensions.

The main viewer still sizes itself directly with 100vh/100dvh. On iOS Safari that can disagree with the visible viewport and causes clipped bottoms, blank strips, or content hidden behind browser chrome. Use the runtime-synchronized viewport height while retaining standards-based fallbacks.

The installed-mode rules currently pin both body and app-shell with position:fixed. Mobile Safari can mis-size fixed root containers after rotation, keyboard use, app resume, and status-bar changes. Keep the application viewport-contained without relying on a fixed root coordinate system, and strengthen the iOS fullscreen/modal/iframe fallbacks.

The mobile layout mixes parent 100dvh sizing with child rows expressed in dvh, which is particularly fragile in Safari because the child row continues to track Safari's viewport independently of the actual available grid height after safe-area padding. Use percentages of the synchronized parent viewport instead and ensure every nested grid/flex region can shrink without overflowing.

The previous cross-browser fix postponed every non-declaration top-level statement until after all variable initializers. That unintentionally postponed CDE global-publication statements such as `globalThis.__IRANCELL_LMS_INITIAL_STATE__ = IRANCELL_INITIAL_STATE`, while dependent store variables such as the published fixture and boot seed were initialized earlier. Chrome/Edge can appear to work when old persisted data already exists, but a fresh iOS Safari/home-screen storage namespace starts without that cache and therefore boots from the reduced fallback seed instead of the project's complete mock data. Split flattened execution into declarations, ordered initialization/publication, and boot side effects. This preserves deterministic CDE source ordering, avoids TDZ problems, and makes published project seeds/configuration available before stores consume them without adding any IranCell-specific compiler behavior.

Generate separate initialization and boot fragments for every flattened CDE source. Variable initializers and global seed/config publication must retain deterministic source order, while calls such as store `InitLogic()`, application mounting, listeners, timers, and other startup side effects must execute only after initialization of every source file has completed.

Assemble every CDE build in four explicit cross-browser phases: first make all function declarations available, then execute variable initialization and global seed/config publication in deterministic CDE file order, then recover public repository exports, and finally execute application/store boot side effects. This fixes fresh iOS mock-data initialization while retaining the earlier Safari/Firefox protection against premature store boot execution.

Add a generic regression test for the exact fresh-mobile failure mode. A CDE project may construct a large mock/fixture seed in one source, publish it through globalThis/window, and consume that published value while initializing its store in a later source. The publication must occur before the store initializer, while the store's explicit boot call must remain after both. This test prevents future compiler changes from silently dropping complete mock datasets on fresh Safari/PWA storage namespaces.

CDE projects may access localStorage or sessionStorage directly instead of only through the EDUS createStore runtime. Safari/iOS and Firefox can restrict storage access inside srcdoc/sandboxed iframe contexts even when the same project works in Chromium. Rewrite browser-storage references at compile time to the EDUS safe storage facade so this compatibility applies generically to every CDE project rather than requiring project-specific store patches.

Run the storage compatibility rewrite after module syntax has been flattened but before final global normalization and generation. This protects direct storage calls in Core, Page, Component, App, imports.js, and any other CDE source file.

The preview runtime needs a synchronous Storage-compatible facade that works even when iframe storage is blocked. Prefer the same-origin parent page storage on phones because it is the top-level installed application's persistent storage, fall back to iframe storage, and finally fall back to memory hosted on the parent browsing context. Namespace every key by CDE project so different projects cannot corrupt each other's persisted stores. Install the facade before checking for an existing createStore so external EDUS data-store implementations also receive safe window.localStorage/window.sessionStorage access when the browser permits overriding those Window properties.

createStore must consume the already-installed project-safe storage facade rather than reading Window.localStorage again. This guarantees the EDUS store works with the same persistence behavior on Chromium, Firefox, normal iOS Safari, private/restricted iframe contexts, and installed iOS home-screen mode.

Give every preview runtime a stable project identity before the storage compatibility runtime starts so storage is isolated per CDE project. Also make the preview document itself use the full mobile viewport and safe areas instead of depending on desktop iframe assumptions.
The safe storage runtime must know which CDE project owns the preview before any project code or data-store code runs.

viewport-fit alone does not make an iOS home-screen launch behave as an installed fullscreen application. Add the Apple standalone metadata, modern mobile web-app metadata, theme colors, and the generated web app manifest used by Vercel production builds.

Vercel needs a real web-app manifest in the generated static deployment for Android/Chromium home-screen installation and modern display-mode negotiation. Generate it as part of the existing Vite static publishing step without introducing another source file. fullscreen is preferred, with standalone as the compatibility fallback used by mobile browsers that do not support fullscreen display mode.

Installed mobile web apps need the document root pinned to the standalone viewport rather than allowing browser viewport resizing to create blank strips around the application. Keep safe-area support and include the WebKit fill-available fallback for older iOS home-screen runtimes.

The viewer combines independently-authored CDE files into one classic global script. Preserving top-level const/let/class declarations gives that generated script temporal-dead-zone and duplicate-lexical-binding behavior that does not belong to the CDE flattened-global contract. It is also the underlying reason project boot functions such as IrancellCoreStoreV2InitLogic can fail depending on browser/runtime ordering. Normalize only the flattened top level to classic var-style globals and separate executable top-level statements so project boot code can be delayed until definitions from every CDE source are ready.

After imports and exports have been normalized, capture top-level execution statements separately from declarations. This makes calls, IIFEs, event registration, boot logic, and other global execution run only after all CDE implementation files have established their shared declarations. The generated declaration code remains in the normal flattened scope, so existing CDE global symbol semantics are preserved.

The old merger executed every file completely as soon as it was concatenated and only recovered exports at the very end. That means a Core file can call its initializer before another Core declaration or shared repository symbol has initialized. Build the output in three deterministic phases instead: declarations/initializers, export recovery, then deferred top-level execution. Also track both normal and deferred source ranges correctly for diagnostics.

The compiler currently explicitly targets Chrome 100, so its generated output is allowed to contain syntax and transformations selected only for Chromium. That contradicts the viewer requirement to execute the same compiled CDE on Firefox, desktop Safari, and iOS Safari. Compile against a conservative shared browser baseline instead.

Safari/iOS Safari and Firefox can restrict localStorage or sessionStorage for sandboxed/srcdoc documents, private browsing, or other privacy contexts. The current compatibility store evaluates global.localStorage before entering readStorage's try block, so the browser can throw before the fallback has a chance to run. Resolve browser storage defensively and make persistence optional rather than allowing a CDE project to fail during store initialization.

Persistence currently re-reads global.localStorage/global.sessionStorage each time and can throw on browsers that expose the property but deny access. Reuse the safely resolved storage handles and silently operate as an in-memory store when persistent browser storage is unavailable.

Add compiler-level regression coverage for the actual architecture bug: a CDE file may contain an eager top-level boot call that uses a declaration supplied by another flattened file, and multiple independently parsed files may use the same top-level lexical alias. These tests ensure future fixes remain generic and do not regress into project-specific patches.

The remaining stack ends at IrancellCoreStoreV2BuildModels -> global code, which means model construction is still executing eagerly while the flattened CDE script is evaluating. Even though the boot seed is declared earlier in the original source, flattened CDE execution can expose initialization-order hazards. Keep one stable models array for exported references, populate it lazily after IrancellCoreStoreV2State is initialized, and use that initialized state as the model seed.
The underlying data-store must trigger lazy model creation when it is actually ready rather than consuming the previously eager global model result.
getModel must also work before or without successful underlying createStore initialization. Ensure the stable exported model array has been populated before searching it.

The runtime stack fails while IrancellCoreStoreV2BuildModels calls IrancellCoreStoreV2ReadPublishedSeed during global script initialization. The published/local seed has already been completely resolved into IRANCELL_CORE_STORE_V2_BOOT_SEED before store state and models are created, so re-evaluating LOCAL_STORE_MODE and LOCAL_SEED during global initialization is unnecessary and can hit lexical initialization ordering in the flattened CDE runtime. Read from the already-normalized boot seed instead while retaining the safe seed as a defensive fallback.

Model definitions are created at top-level while the flattened CDE script is booting. They must use the already-resolved boot seed directly instead of invoking a runtime seed resolver during global evaluation. This removes the IrancellCoreStoreV2ReadPublishedSeed -> IrancellCoreStoreV2BuildModels -> global code failure path while preserving the same fixture/remote seed selected earlier by IRANCELL_CORE_STORE_V2_BOOT_SEED.
